clue.text: ELP's essential content, in full colour

definitions.meaning: ELP is the band Emerson; its central letter L stands for the middle member, Greg, whose surname written out in full fills the light
a crimson pigment made from dye fixed on a base

explanation.surface: A music critic reviews the core of an ELP record in glorious full colour.
explanation.walkthrough: ELP is the 1970s prog-rock trio Emerson, Lake and Palmer: the middle initial L, spelt out in full, is the bassist's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A lake is a red pigment, a dye precipitated onto a mineral base, used as an artist's colour.

clue.text: Lion seen in a Times listing

indicators.note: something seen in a place sits inside it, so the lion goes within the other letters

parts.note: T stands for time, and times plural gives two of them, TT
Aslan is the lion in C S Lewis's Narnia books

explanation.surface: A lion turns up in a newspaper's listings page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Times' looks like the London newspaper, but it is simply 'a' followed by the plural of a time abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something listing leans to one side, tilted off the vertical, like a ship heeling over.

clue.text: Get out of bed, perhaps, to drive a coach and horses through …

definitions.meaning: read playfully as ..., to take someone off their bunk, a kind of bed

definitions.text: to drive a coach and horses through
definitions.meaning: an idiom for demolishing an argument or claim by exposing its flaws

explanation.surface: Someone rises from bed to drive a coach and horses, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is whimsical: DE- as removal plus BUNK, a bed. The trailing dots join this clue to the next one's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing a myth as false wrecks it, just as driving a coach and horses through a rule does.

clue.text: … a day taking rides around Greek islands

indicators.note: the outer word takes in, or holds, the shorter pieces
the word for rides goes around the other letters, confirming the containment

parts.note: bike rides are cycles

explanation.surface: A holiday day spent on bike rides around the Greek islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclades are an Aegean archipelago including Mykonos, Naxos and Santorini.

clue.text: Ceremonial observance of union in Iranian capital

indicators.note: the union letters are placed in the currency word

parts.note: capital here means money: the rial is the currency of Iran
TU is short for trade union

explanation.surface: A marriage ceremony being held in Tehran, Iran's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' wants to be Tehran; it means money, so it is the rial.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a ceremonial observance performed in a fixed, solemn, prescribed way.

clue.text: Look at part of golf course that's out of bounds

indicators.note: the bounds of a word are its two ends, so both outer letters are put out

parts.note: a dogleg is a hole on a golf course that bends sharply partway along

explanation.surface: A golfer inspects a stretch of the course where the ball would be out of bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of bounds' is golf language in the surface; here it strips the first and last letters, D and G, from DOGLEG.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer or stare at someone admiringly is a way of looking at them.

clue.text: LP the writer regularly plays at her raves

indicators.note: raving is wild and disordered, so these letters are rearranged
taking every other letter of the word plays, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Someone plays a long-playing record at her wild parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'LP' looks like a record; it is the initials of L. P. Hartley, author of The Go-Between. 'regularly' gives LY from plays; 'raves' shuffles LY with AT HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Leslie Poles Hartley was an English novelist, author of The Go-Between.

clue.text: Depression of key characters in extremely tricky first half of game

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, first and last
only the opening half of the game's name is kept

parts.note: ping-pong is another name for table tennis

explanation.surface: A sense of gloom among the key players in a tricky first half of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like low mood but means pressing down; 'key characters' are letters on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyboard work consists of pressing down keys to produce letters on a page or screen.

clue.text: Tax too much, taking off a third initially

indicators.note: a third of a six-letter word is two letters, removed from its start

parts.note: an excess is too much of something

explanation.surface: A complaint that taxes are too high and should be cut by a third.
explanation.definitionFit: A cess is an old word for a levy or rate, still used in Ireland and India for a tax.

clue.text: Clean out pond, accompanied by sound of Overture to William Tell

indicators.note: letters put out of order are rearranged
the name of a letter when spoken out
the overture, or opening, of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Pond-cleaning carried out to the strains of Rossini's William Tell Overture.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter of William is W, whose spoken name 'double-u' gives UU. 'out' rearranges POND, UU and TELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something free of contamination or pollution is pure and clean.

clue.text: Playing grand piano briefly in opera, or another instrument

indicators.note: playing with letters means moving them about into a new order

parts.note: GP is a short form of grand piano

explanation.surface: A grand piano being played in an opera, or perhaps some other instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A large keyboard instrument with ranks of pipes, found in churches, is another instrument besides the piano.

clue.text: Chess player with defence partially involving Latvian opening

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or include, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a back is one member, so part, of a team's defence in football

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A chess player whose defence draws partly on the Latvian Gambit opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latvian Gambit is a real chess opening played by the second player, making the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the two sides are named by colour, and the second mover takes the dark pieces.

clue.text: Half-heartedly shout down

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its doubled middle letter, and half of that pair is dropped

parts.note: to bellow is to shout loudly

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly shouts a heckler down.
explanation.walkthrough: BELLOW has LL at its centre; losing one of the two leaves half the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean at a lower level, as in 'see the notes down there' or underneath.

clue.text: Trump at last becoming confused, rowing when little pressure is applied

definitions.text: rowing when little pressure is applied

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: addling means growing muddled or confused

explanation.surface: Donald Trump at last losing his head in a heated row when under little pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rowing' looks like quarrelling; it is the sport, where this term means pulling the oars lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing, the term is used for easy, light strokes taken without full power.

clue.text: Lowest point of floor I dance around

indicators.note: turned around means read the other way
the letters are taken from within, as part of, the phrase

explanation.surface: A dancer hits rock bottom while dancing around the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' marks letters taken from floor I dance, RIDAN, and 'around' turns them to read the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy and figuratively the nadir is the very bottom, the opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: Kitty curls round lecturer in bed

indicators.note: one piece wraps itself round the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a kitty is a pot of shared money, as in a card game

explanation.surface: A cat curls up around a lecturer lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' looks like a cat; it is a pot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden bed is a small piece of ground set aside for planting.

clue.text: Perhaps John B Turner could bet on these ones appearing today

definitions.text: could bet on these ones appearing today

indicators.note: a turner turns things, so the boat's word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: Sloop John B is a Beach Boys song, so John B is an example of a sloop

explanation.surface: A man named John B Turner might place a bet on today's fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John B Turner' looks like a person; 'Perhaps John B' is a sloop, as in the Beach Boys' Sloop John B, and 'Turner' reverses it. The football pools are a British betting game on match results.
explanation.definitionFit: Punters bet on the football pools by predicting results of the day's matches.

clue.text: Monasteries? First concerns, no sex!

indicators.note: the word for sex is not allowed, so it is taken out

parts.note: priorities are the matters that come first
IT is a crossword stand-in for sex appeal, or sex itself

explanation.surface: A monastery's rules: top priority, no sex.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the plural noun as a group of religious houses; IT comes out of PRIORITIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A priory is a religious house headed by a prior, a type of monastery.

clue.text: Bathing beach you'd love, if topless

parts.note: with its top, or lid, removed, so the answer's opening is a word for a top
what remains is love, which is O, nil in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A bathing beach you'd love if you could go topless there.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: take the LID (top) off the answer and you have O, love. So the answer is LID + O.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming place or bathing beach, from the Lido in Venice.

clue.text: Purchase gravel spread with ease, say

indicators.note: the letters are spread about, scattered into a new order
say signals that the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: spoken, the word sounds like the plural of the letter E

explanation.surface: Gravel is spread easily, perhaps when buying a driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying; it means grip or mechanical advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase can mean a firm grip or mechanical advantage, the effect a lever gives.

clue.text: Solicitor General seduces females, according to some feminists' spinning

indicators.note: the outer piece draws the other in, taking it inside

parts.note: SG is the abbreviation for Solicitor General
wimmin is a spelling of women used by some feminists to avoid the word men

explanation.surface: A senior law officer seduces women, as some feminists' spin would have it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' looks like media spin; it means dizzy, as in a head reeling.
explanation.definitionFit: When a head is reeling with dizziness, it is said to swim or be spinning.

clue.text: Welsh woman with English car

parts.note: Megan is a common Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman drives an English car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mégane is a family hatchback made by the French firm Renault.

clue.text: Organ intro missing from musical

indicators.note: the introduction, or first letter, of the show's name is left off

parts.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's musical based on Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: An organ introduction is missing from the score of a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' looks like the instrument of the surface; it is the body organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's largest internal gland, which filters the blood, is an organ.

clue.text: Sailor seen in Carla's caring embrace

indicators.note: the word is visible within the run of letters
the two clue words hold the word between them, across the gap

explanation.surface: A sailor is found in Carla's loving embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A lascar was a sailor from India or Southeast Asia serving on European ships.

clue.text: Transcribed essential part of Nina Simone's ultimate Strange Fruit

indicators.note: a transcribed piece of music is arranged afresh, so these letters are rearranged
the essential part of a word is its middle, the letters without the ends
the ultimate letter of a word is its last

explanation.surface: A transcription of Nina Simone's famous recording of Strange Fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange Fruit' looks like the song title; Strange is fodder and Fruit the definition. 'Transcribed' rearranges IN, E and STRANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Small loose-skinned mandarin oranges with deep orange skin are a citrus fruit.

clue.text: Host that's daft, but not soft in the head

indicators.note: the soft letter is not to be kept
the letter removed is at the head, the start, of the word

parts.note: barmy means daft or crazy
B marks a soft pencil lead, as against H for hard

explanation.surface: A host who is daft, but not soft in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft in the head' looks like an idiom for silly; B is the soft pencil grade, removed from the head of BARMY.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great number, especially a multitude of soldiers, as in a heavenly host.

clue.text: Studies disheartened Labour party members?

indicators.note: the heart, or central letter, of the word is removed

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it, especially at university

explanation.surface: A study showing Labour Party members feeling disheartened.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that only some Labour members are left-wing enough to count.
explanation.definitionFit: Left-wingers or socialists are nicknamed after the colour of the left's banners.

clue.text: Spring flower

definitions.meaning: to spring is to move suddenly and fast, to dash forward
read as flow-er, something that flows: a river, here the Devon river of that name

explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' looks like a bloom, as 'Spring' suggests; it is a river, the one in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot forward suddenly is to spring; a river in Devon is a flower.

clue.text: Day important for primate

parts.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monday, a day
key means important or crucial

explanation.surface: A day that matters for a primate.
explanation.definitionFit: Apes, lemurs and humans are primates, as are long-tailed tree-dwelling simians.

clue.text: Which clothes might be put on in hotel close to city in Western France?

definitions.text: Which clothes might be put on

indicators.note: the hotel sits close to, right beside, the city

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Angers is a city on the Maine in the Loire valley of western France

explanation.surface: A question about what to wear in a hotel near a city in western France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' looks like dressing; here clothes are put on a rack of hooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaped wire or wooden frames hold clothes up in a wardrobe; clothes are put on them.
